elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer (preferred)
elements.evidence: "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory."

elements.element: No field-of-use / territory restriction on Customer's business (preferred)
elements.evidence: § 12.3 "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory"; amended § 12.4 now permissive "in any territory"

elements.element: Restriction limited to a single named competing product (fallback)
elements.evidence: Amended text still refers to "any product or service that competes with Vendor" — no named product, though it is now a permission, not a restriction
"During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" retained in the (now permissive) sentence

elements.element: Carve-out for internal development and acquisitions (fallback)
elements.evidence: No carve-out language inserted; instead the prohibition itself was converted to "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire"

reasons: The single operator change from "shall not" to "may" eliminates the non-compete and field-of-use restriction on Customer, satisfying the locked preferred position.
The edit is the minimum sufficient change: one verb phrase replaced, no boilerplate added, no clause rewritten, and no requirement imported from the fallback level.

Fallback elements (named product, term-only, 12-month cap, internal development and acquisition carve-outs) are not present, but they are unnecessary because the preferred level (no restriction at all) is achieved; the two bargains were not mixed.

Intent preserved: the amended sentence now aligns with § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no non-compete commitment, removing the internal contradiction; no undefined terms or dangling mechanics introduced.

Note (not a deviation under this rule): the separate § 12.4 no-solicit/no-hire obligation for twenty-four months remains and still conflicts with § 12.3's "no ... no-hire commitment" acknowledgement; that is a non-solicit issue outside the NONCOMPETE rule and pre-existing, not created by this edit.
